items.followUp: Define intermolecular forces and explain how hydrogen bonding occurs between water molecules.

rubric.description: Intermolecular forces are attractive forces between molecules.
rubric.how: Award for identifying both that the forces are attractive and that they act between molecules.

rubric.why: States the condition that allows hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is bonded to a highly electronegative atom such as oxygen, nitrogen, or fluorine.
rubric.how: Award for identifying hydrogen bonded to at least one of oxygen, nitrogen, or fluorine.

rubric.why: Explains the attraction that forms a hydrogen bond.
rubric.description: The partially positive hydrogen is attracted to a lone pair on an electronegative atom of a neighboring molecule.
rubric.how: Award for linking the partially positive hydrogen to a lone pair on another molecule.

rubric.why: Provides an example or a physical-property effect of hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Identifies hydrogen bonding between water molecules or states that hydrogen bonding raises boiling point.
rubric.how: Award for either the water example or the correct boiling-point effect.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are attractive forces that act between molecules and are generally weaker than the bonds within molecules.
Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is bonded to a highly electronegative atom such as oxygen, nitrogen, or fluorine.
The partially positive hydrogen is attracted to a lone pair on an electronegative atom of a neighboring molecule.
Hydrogen bonds form between water molecules.
Hydrogen bonding can raise a substance’s boiling point.

items.followUp: Give one characteristic of a homogeneous mixture and one characteristic of a heterogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: States the defining composition of a homogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its composition is uniform or the same throughout.

rubric.why: States the defining composition or appearance of a heterogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, with distinguishable components or phases.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is non-uniform or that its components or phases can be distinguished.

modelAnswer: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout.
A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, and its components or phases can be distinguished.

items.followUp: Define a molecule and molecular mass.

rubric.why: Defines a formula unit in terms of the ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.description: A formula unit represents the simplest whole-number ratio of positive and negative ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the formula unit as the simplest whole-number ratio of ions.

rubric.why: Defines formula mass as the sum of the relevant atomic masses.
rubric.description: Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms represented in a formula unit.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the atomic masses represented in the formula unit are added.

modelAnswer: A formula unit is the simplest whole-number ratio of positive and negative ions in an ionic compound.
Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms represented in the formula unit.
